title: Use of turmeric in wound healing
status: revoked — revoked in 1997 by the USPTO following a reexamination request filed by India's Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
abstract: Patent claiming the use of turmeric (Curcuma longa) powder for promoting the healing of wounds.
description: Challenged by CSIR on the ground that turmeric's use for wound healing was traditional knowledge already known and practiced in India and therefore lacked novelty. CSIR's reexamination request included documentary evidence of prior use, including a reference to ancient Sanskrit texts and a 1953 paper in the Journal of the Indian Medical Association. The USPTO revoked the patent in 1997, finding no novelty. This is the canonical example, worldwide, of traditional knowledge defeating a granted patent — use it as the flagship illustration when explaining Section 3(p) and the purpose of TKDL/prior-art documentation to a user.
data_quality_note: Patent number, applicant, inventors, subject matter, CSIR challenge, evidence used, and 1997 revocation are corroborated across multiple independent sources. Exact filing/grant day-month dates were not confirmed with enough precision here — pull the exact dates from the Google Patents / USPTO record at source_url before citing a specific date to a user.

title: Hydrophobic extracted neem oil: method of preparation and use
applicant: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) and W.R. Grace & Co.
status: revoked — revoked by the EPO Opposition Division in May 2000 on grounds of lack of novelty/inventive step following a biopiracy challenge; revocation upheld on appeal by the EPO Technical Board of Appeal on 2005-03-08
abstract: Patent covering a hydrophobic solvent-extraction method for producing storage-stable neem oil formulations with fungicidal/insecticidal properties.
description: Challenged by a coalition including the European Parliament's Green Party, India's Research Foundation for Science, Technology and Ecology (led by Vandana Shiva), and the International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movements, on the ground that neem's fungicidal/pesticidal properties and extraction were traditional knowledge long practiced in India, and that the claimed extraction process lacked an inventive step over that known use. This was the first patent revoked by the EPO explicitly on biopiracy grounds. Use alongside the turmeric case as a second, internationally-notable example — this one specifically demonstrates that traditional-knowledge prior art can defeat a patent outside India too, which matters for the international-jurisdiction half of the assistant.
data_quality_note: Publication number, publication date, applicants, challengers, revocation grounds, May 2000 revocation, and 2005-03-08 appeal outcome are corroborated across multiple independent sources (CORDIS, contemporaneous news wire). Exact grant date not confirmed — pull from the EPO register at the source_url before citing precisely.

title: Basmati rice lines and grains
status: narrowed — following USPTO reexamination prompted by challenges from the Indian government and NGOs (including the Research Foundation for Science, Technology and Ecology and the Centre for Food Safety), RiceTec withdrew/lost 15 of the original 20 claims in 2001; the remaining claims and the patent's title were narrowed to cover three specific bred rice lines (Bas 867, RT1117, RT1121) rather than 'Basmati' generally, and do not affect Basmati grown in India
abstract: Patent originally claiming novel basmati-type rice lines and grains, including broad use of the term 'Basmati', developed by crossbreeding traditional basmati varieties with a semi-dwarf rice variety.
description: This is a Geographical-Indication / naming dispute as much as a patentability one — India's core objection was that 'Basmati' denotes rice of a specific geographic origin (the Indo-Gangetic plains) and that RiceTec's use of the name for a US-grown crossbred variety was misleading, alongside prior-art objections to some claims. Useful in IP-SAKTI as the flagship example distinguishing GI-type concerns from patent novelty concerns — a single dispute can raise both, and the classifier/router should be able to explain that distinction to a user rather than treating it as a single undifferentiated 'IP issue'.
source_authority: contemporaneous reporting corroborated across multiple independent sources
data_quality_note: Filing date (1994-07-08), grant date (1997-09-02), 20 original claims, 15 claims cancelled in 2001, and the three remaining rice-line names are corroborated across multiple independent sources including a contemporaneous news report quoting the Indian government's official statement to Parliament. High confidence on this record.
